week_in_history.narrative:
This one gets dug up because it's the tightest Week 8 finish the league has ever recorded — a 3.52-point gap, which is close enough that both of these guys probably felt something in their chest when the final scores posted. Salmation Nation's Josh Davis walked away with the win, 116.82 to 113.3, and if he enjoyed it, he should have savored every second, because the wheels came off immediately after. Davis closed out 2023 by going 1-5 the rest of the way and missing the playoffs entirely, turning a promising October squeaker into a cautionary tale by December.

Brian Harris, meanwhile, took the tough loss on the chin and quietly put together the better season. The Tomahawk Piranhas went 3-3 down the stretch, snuck into the postseason, and actually made some noise before getting bounced in the quarterfinal. Funny how that works — lose the closest game in Week 8 history and still end up the one with a real season.

weekly_recap.previous_weekend: John Schauder squeaked past Brian Kleinhenz 119.38 to 117.1, a 2.28-point margin that's gonna sting Brian for a solid week — especially since this stays locked in his memory, unlike whatever happens in that mysterious whiskey room nobody's allowed to ask about. Trey McBride's 24.1 points carried Schauder's roster while the Texans D/ST contributed a goose egg, and somehow it was still enough. Jameson Williams dropped 23.6 for Brian, and Javonte Williams went off for 23.5 on Monday night trying to save the day — but with Kansas City's defense bleeding a negative point total, it was dead weight he couldn't drag across the finish line. This is their fourth all-time meeting, and Brian still leads the head-to-head 2-1, but that career 55.1 winning percentage isn't going to feel like much when "always the bridesmaid" Schauder — three seasons in, zero playoff appearances, zero rings — finally crashes somebody's wedding and walks off with a win instead of a consolation prize.
weekly_recap.honorable_mention: Not quite the marquee matchup, but the next-closest game of the week still gave us something worth stapling to the bulletin board: Brian Harris outlasting Daniel Bahamonde 115.4 to 105.82, a 9.58-point margin that felt bigger once Dominic Zvada face-planted for a measly 2.0 points for Daniel. Jonathan Taylor's 18.0-point outing for Brian did the heavy lifting while Daniel's lineup quietly imploded. This was their seventh all-time meeting, and Brian now leads the series 4-3. Daniel's claim to fame remains a Taylor Swift photo — still more memorable than his 36.7 career winning percentage and his career-long search for a playoff appearance that doesn't exist.
weekly_recap.game_of_the_week: Two 5-2 squads, one shared parking spot in the standings, and a series tied 2-2 all-time that's about to get its fifth and most annoyingly even chapter. Eddie's "She's Tuten from Herbert" sits ranked 2nd overall, averaging 114.73 points a game this season, backed by a power score that's actually the 2nd best in the league — the banjo-and-kick-drum enthusiast is thriving despite a career championship count stuck at zero across three complete seasons. Jay's "High Quality H2O," the trusted commissioner nobody elected but everybody tolerates, is ranked 3rd with a thinner 108.05 scoring average this season and a power rank of just 7th — numbers that don't scream contender so much as whisper it nervously into a conference call mute button. Jay's luck factor sits at a gaudy 0.2208, meaning his record is flattering him hard. Eddie's 99.0% playoff probability dwarfs Jay's 91.0%, and this one should settle the tiebreaker with authority.
